## Reading a clip

Each clip is drawn as one rounded block with a thin border, so you can see
where one ends and the next begins.

- **Colour by kind**: video slate, audio green, image or still violet, text
  amber, shape teal (graphics use the same colour), nest grey, adjustment
  rose.
- **Name strip** along the top: a symbol for the kind, then the clip's name.
  A clip with no name of its own shows what it holds: its file, its text, its
  shape or its nest.
- **Label dot**: a labelled clip gets a small dot in its label colour at the
  right end of the name strip. The block's colour still shows its kind.
- **Filmstrip**: thumbnails along the picture part of a video or image clip,
  under a wash of the clip's colour. Each thumbnail is the source frame at
  that point, following speed, reverse and speed ramps.
- **Waveform**: the sound of a clip that has audio, drawn below the
  filmstrip on a clip that has both. Muted, or silenced by another track's
  solo, it draws faded.
- **Fade handles**: small white squares at the top corners of the audio part.
  Drag one inward to fade (see [Audio](audio.md)).
- **Volume line**: a thin white line over the waveform showing the level you
  hear from the clip, with small squares where a volume action ends. Drag it
  to change the level, or ⌥-click it to add a point (see
  [Audio](audio.md#the-volume-line)). A silenced clip's line lies along the
  bottom.
- **Motion marks**: small wedges at the ends of the name strip for an active
  In or Out motion, and a wave glyph for a During motion (see
  [Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md)).
- **Transitions**: the overlap between two clips is hatched, with the
  transition's kind written in it when the word fits.
- **Selected**: a 2 pt coral ring, with trim grips at both ends when the clip
  is wide enough to trim and its track is unlocked.
- **Linked**: a picture and the sound Detach Audio split from it each show a
  link symbol after the kind symbol. When one is selected, the other gets a
  dashed accent ring, because edits to one move both (see
  [Audio](audio.md#what-stays-in-sync)).
- **Dimmed**: a clip on a hidden track, or one with both its picture and its
  sound switched off.
- **No filmstrip**: text, shape, graphic, nest and adjustment clips have no
  thumbnails. An adjustment clip is a plain rose block with only its name
  strip and action lane, and its track is sized as a picture track.

Filmstrips and waveforms come from a cache made for each media file after
import, so they fill in a moment after a file is added.

### The action lane

A clip that has actions (keyframed segments) gets an **action lane** right
under its name strip. Each action is a band. At Medium and Large each band
shows its number in time order (and a zoom glyph for a zoom action); at Large
it also lists the properties it changes; at Small the bands are plain bars.
The selected action is solid, its span is washed down the clip, and it is
shaded on the ruler.

Hover a band to highlight it and show its 5 pt grips at both ends (a band
15 pt wide or less has none). The pointer is an open hand over the body and
a resize arrow over a grip.

Click a band to select the clip and that action; the playhead also moves to
the action's end, so the preview shows its end state. Drag a band's body to
move the action, or drag a grip to resize it. After a move or resize the
action stays selected and the playhead goes to its new end. When exactly one
clip is selected, playing or scrubbing into one of its actions' spans
selects that action. Esc leaves it, and ⌫ removes it.
Everything else about actions is on
[Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md).

## The ruler and the playhead

The ruler's ticks adjust to the zoom, from single frames up to minutes.
Labels drop the hours when the timeline is under an hour long. The playhead
is the coral line with a triangle head on the ruler.

- **Click the ruler** to move the playhead there, and **drag** along it to
  scrub. Playback stops while you scrub, and you hear the sound under the
  playhead instead (see [Hearing a scrub](audio.md#hearing-a-scrub)). The
  scrub snaps like any other drag
  (see [Snapping](#snapping)).
- The timeline scrolls itself to keep the playhead in view: when the playhead

3	/// One clip, drawn as ONE OBJECT (the redesign's §3).
4	///
5	/// The old bar had no boundary: the filmstrip and the waveform ran edge to
6	/// edge as two stacked bands and the name sat in a black strip that read as
7	/// part of the image, so you could not see where one clip ended and the next
8	/// began. What replaces it is a body — inset 3 pt from the lane, rounded,
9	/// clipped, with a 1 pt light border — carrying a 16 pt name strip along its
10	/// top and the media UNDER a wash of the clip's own tint, so a filmstrip reads
11	/// as a tinted clip rather than as a strip of photographs.
12	///
13	/// The alpha washes here are white-over-tint and black-over-tint literals
14	/// (0.14 border, 0.26 strip, 0.44 waveform, 0.54 wash, 0.62/0.72/0.92 inks).
15	/// They are deliberately NOT `DS` tokens: each is relative to the clip tint
16	/// underneath it, which is a fixed ink in both appearances, so a semantic
17	/// colour would break the contrast the design chose.
18	///
19	/// This is an extension of `TimelineContentView` — `TimelineView.swift` is
20	/// frozen at wiring (app/CLAUDE.md) and this is where the redesign's work
21	/// went.
22	extension TimelineContentView {
23	    /// The clip's body: the lane rect inset 3 pt top and bottom, which is the
24	    /// gap that makes two lanes read as two rows of objects.
25	    static func bodyRect(_ rect: CGRect) -> CGRect {
26	        CGRect(
27	            x: rect.minX, y: rect.minY + 3, width: rect.width,
28	            height: max(rect.height - 6, 1))
29	    }
30	
31	    /// The body under the name strip — where the filmstrip, the waveform and
32	    /// the fade handles live.
33	    ///
34	    /// The HIT TEST reads this too (`TimelineContentView.hit(at:)` looks for a
35	    /// fade handle at the audio region's corner): the handles moved down by
36	    /// the strip's height when the body arrived, and a hit test still measuring
37	    /// from the lane's top edge would leave them undraggable.
38	    static func contentRect(_ rect: CGRect) -> CGRect {
39	        let body = bodyRect(rect)
40	        return CGRect(
41	            x: body.minX, y: body.minY + DS.clipHeaderHeight, width: body.width,
42	            height: max(body.height - DS.clipHeaderHeight, 0))
43	    }

45	    /// One track's clips in three passes: every body, then every transition
46	    /// zone, then every selection ring. A zone starts at `clip.start` and so
47	    /// lies inside the PREVIOUS clip's body, over its right edge: drawn with
48	    /// that clip, the NEXT clip's hatch painted white 0.26 and a solid white
49	    /// edge straight over the previous clip's ring (#66). Clips outside
50	    /// `dirtyRect` are skipped in every pass. On a matte track the first two
51	    /// passes run at half opacity inside `drawMatteLane` (spec §11 MT-7,
52	    /// `TimelineView+Matte.swift`); the rings stay whole.
53	    func drawClips(
54	        _ clips: [ClipSnapshot], row: Int, track: TrackSnapshot, owner: TimelineView,
55	        dirtyRect: CGRect
56	    ) {
57	        let rects = clips.map { owner.layout.clipRect($0, row: row) }
58	        let shown = clips.indices.filter { rects[$0].intersects(dirtyRect) }
59	        drawMatteLane(
60	            track: track, rects: shown.map { rects[$0] },
61	            lane: owner.layout.rowRect(row, width: owner.layout.contentWidth), owner: owner
62	        ) {
63	            for i in shown {
64	                draw(clip: clips[i], in: rects[i], track: track, owner: owner, visible: dirtyRect)
65	            }
66	            for i in shown where i > 0 {
67	                drawTransition(
68	                    clips[i], previous: clips[i - 1], in: Self.bodyRect(rects[i]),
69	                    layout: owner.layout)
70	            }
71	        }
72	        for i in shown where owner.selection.contains(clips[i].id) {
73	            drawSelectionRing(Self.bodyRect(rects[i]))
74	        }
75	        // The echo: a selected clip's linked partner, which the core moves
76	        // with it, gets a dashed accent ring (spec §11 AU-97). A partner
77	        // that is itself selected has its own ring.
78	        for i in shown {
79	            guard let partner = clips[i].linked, owner.selection.contains(partner),
80	                  !owner.selection.contains(clips[i].id)
81	            else { continue }
82	            drawEchoRing(Self.bodyRect(rects[i]))
83	        }
84	    }

86	    /// One clip's body, in paint order: fill, media, the selected action's
87	    /// wash, name strip, action lane, fade handles, grips and border. Its
88	    /// transition zone and its selection ring are `drawClips`'s later passes.
89	    private func draw(
90	        clip: ClipSnapshot, in rect: CGRect, track: TrackSnapshot, owner: TimelineView,
91	        visible: CGRect
92	    ) {
93	        let layout = owner.layout
94	        let body = Self.bodyRect(rect)
95	        let dimmed = track.hidden || (!clip.enabled.video && !clip.enabled.audio)
96	        var tint = ClipKindStyle.tint(for: clip, in: owner.snapshot)
97	        if dimmed {
98	            tint = tint.blended(withFraction: 0.5, of: DS.chromeBackground) ?? tint
99	        }
100	
101	        NSGraphicsContext.current?.saveGraphicsState()
102	        NSBezierPath(
103	            roundedRect: body, xRadius: TimelineLayout.clipRadius,
104	            yRadius: TimelineLayout.clipRadius
105	        ).addClip()
106	        tint.setFill()
107	        body.fill()
108	
109	        // Everything below the name strip. At the Small text lane (30 pt) this
110	        // is a sliver, which the design says is correct: a clip there IS its
111	        // name strip.
112	        let content = Self.contentRect(rect)
113	
114	        let hasVideo = owner.hasVideo(clip)
115	        let hasAudio = owner.hasAudio(clip)
116	        let regions = Self.regions(in: content, hasVideo: hasVideo, hasAudio: hasAudio)
117	        if !regions.video.isEmpty {
118	            drawFilmstrip(clip, in: regions.video, tint: tint, owner: owner, visible: visible)
119	        }
120	        if !regions.audio.isEmpty {
121	            // Silent is what the core mixes as silent (`audio.rs`'s
122	            // `silenced`): muted, or some OTHER track in the container soloed.
123	            // The header's M stays unlit under a solo — it shows the switch —
124	            // but the waveform shows the mix. Nested clips are never drawn
125	            // here, so the container is always the timeline's own track set.
126	            let silencedBySolo = owner.snapshot.tracks.contains { $0.solo } && !track.solo
127	            let muted = clip.audioProps.muted || track.muted || silencedBySolo
128	            drawWaveform(clip, in: regions.audio, owner: owner, visible: visible, muted: muted)
129	            drawDuckCurve(clip, in: regions.audio, owner: owner, visible: visible)
130	            drawVolumeLine(clip, rect: rect, owner: owner, visible: visible)
131	        }
132	        drawGateLine(clip, in: regions.video, owner: owner, visible: visible)
133	        drawActionWash(clip, body: body, owner: owner)
134	        drawNameStrip(clip, in: body, owner: owner)
135	        drawActionBands(clip, rect: rect, owner: owner)
136	
137	        if hasAudio, regions.audio.height >= TimelineLayout.fadeHandle + 2 {
138	            for edge in [TimelineEdge.start, TimelineEdge.end] {
139	                let handle = Self.fadeRect(clip, edge: edge, audio: regions.audio, layout: layout)
140	                NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.7).setFill()
141	                handle.fill()
142	            }
143	        }
144	
145	        // Trim grips are a DRAWING, not a hit target: `TimelineLayout.edgeGrab`
146	        // stays 7 pt, so making these 6 pt bars the grab zone would shrink an
147	        // affordance that already works. They appear on the selected clip only
148	        // so an unselected timeline stays quiet.
149	        //
150	        // The threshold is the HIT TEST's, not the grip's own width: `hit(at:)`
151	        // and `resetCursorRects` both give up on a bar narrower than
152	        // `edgeGrab * 3` (21 pt), and a grip drawn on a 19 pt clip would be an
153	        // affordance that cannot be grabbed. `body.width` is `rect.width` —
154	        // `bodyRect` insets only top and bottom — so this is the same number
155	        // the hit test measures. A LOCKED track is excluded for the same
156	        // reason: `hit(at:)` returns `.clip` there before it ever reaches the
157	        // width test, so a grip drawn on one could only lie.
158	        if owner.selection.contains(clip.id), !track.locked,
159	           body.width > TimelineLayout.edgeGrab * 3 {
160	            NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.38).setFill()
161	            NSRect(
162	                x: body.minX, y: body.minY, width: DS.trimGripWidth, height: body.height
163	            ).fill()
164	            NSRect(
165	                x: body.maxX - DS.trimGripWidth, y: body.minY, width: DS.trimGripWidth,
166	                height: body.height
167	            ).fill()
168	        }
169	        NSGraphicsContext.current?.restoreGraphicsState()
170	
171	        let border = NSBezierPath(
172	            roundedRect: body.insetBy(dx: 0.5, dy: 0.5), xRadius: TimelineLayout.clipRadius,
173	            yRadius: TimelineLayout.clipRadius)
174	        border.lineWidth = 1
175	        NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.14).setStroke()
176	        border.stroke()
177	    }

179	    /// The selected clip's 2 pt coral ring, inside its body's edge. Painted in
180	    /// `drawClips`' last pass, so no transition hatch lies over it.
181	    private func drawSelectionRing(_ body: CGRect) {
182	        DS.playhead.setStroke()
183	        let outline = NSBezierPath(
184	            roundedRect: body.insetBy(dx: 1, dy: 1), xRadius: TimelineLayout.clipRadius,
185	            yRadius: TimelineLayout.clipRadius)
186	        outline.lineWidth = 2
187	        outline.stroke()
188	    }

190	    /// A selected clip's linked partner: the selection ring's geometry,
191	    /// dashed, in the accent.
192	    private func drawEchoRing(_ body: CGRect) {
193	        DS.accent.setStroke()
194	        let outline = NSBezierPath(
195	            roundedRect: body.insetBy(dx: 1, dy: 1), xRadius: TimelineLayout.clipRadius,
196	            yRadius: TimelineLayout.clipRadius)
197	        outline.lineWidth = 2
198	        outline.setLineDash([4, 3], count: 2, phase: 0)
199	        outline.stroke()
200	    }

202	    // MARK: - Name strip
203	
204	    /// The 16 pt strip along the body's top: a black wash over the tint, the
205	    /// kind symbol, the name truncated with an ellipsis, and — when the clip
206	    /// carries a label — a 6 pt dot in the label's colour at the right end.
207	    /// The kind symbol is the point of it — a clip's kind used to be
208	    /// invisible. The label is a DOT and never the tint: the tint says what a
209	    /// clip IS (spec §4.4's six inks, which the washes below are calibrated
210	    /// for), and a label is something the user said about it.
211	    private func drawNameStrip(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, in body: CGRect, owner: TimelineView) {
212	        let strip = CGRect(
213	            x: body.minX, y: body.minY, width: body.width,
214	            height: min(DS.clipHeaderHeight, body.height))
215	        NSColor.black.withAlphaComponent(0.26).setFill()
216	        strip.fill()
217	        // `hasPixels` is the test the Motion section and Clip ▸ Motion gate
218	        // on: a detached audio twin clones the video props, and its strip
219	        // must not claim a motion it never shows.
220	        let motion = InspectorTab.hasPixels(clip, in: owner.snapshot) ? clip.videoProps.motion : nil
221	        if let motion = motion {
222	            drawMotionWedges(motion, clip: clip, strip: strip, body: body)
223	        }
224	
225	        let padding: CGFloat = 6
226	        var x = strip.minX + padding
227	        var nameEnd = strip.maxX - padding
228	        let symbol = ClipKindStyle.symbol(for: clip, in: owner.snapshot)
229	        let iconBox = CGRect(x: x, y: strip.minY, width: 11, height: strip.height)
230	        if iconBox.maxX <= strip.maxX - padding {
231	            TimelineDraw.symbol(
232	                symbol.name, fallback: symbol.fallback, in: iconBox,
233	                tint: NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.62))
234	            x = iconBox.maxX + 5
235	        }
236	        // A linked clip (Detach Audio's picture or sound, spec §11 AU-97):
237	        // the link glyph right after the kind, guarded like it.
238	        let linkBox = CGRect(x: x, y: strip.minY, width: 11, height: strip.height)
239	        if clip.linked != nil, linkBox.maxX <= strip.maxX - padding {
240	            TimelineDraw.symbol(
241	                "link", fallback: "∞", in: linkBox,
242	                tint: NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.62))
243	            x = linkBox.maxX + 5
244	        }
245	        // Guarded like the icon: a strip too narrow for both keeps the kind
246	        // and drops the dot, rather than painting one over its own edge. The
247	        // name gives up the dot's 6 pt plus the icon's 5 pt gap for it. Any
248	        // non-empty label draws — an unknown name in the neutral ink — so a
249	        // project from a newer build still shows WHERE its labels are.
250	        // Where the dot's own left edge landed, or nil when no dot drew. The
251	        // glyph below needs THAT, and `nameEnd` is not it: `nameEnd` is where
252	        // the NAME stops, which three different branches move.
253	        var dotLeft: CGFloat?
254	        if let label = clip.label, !label.isEmpty {
255	            let dot = CGRect(
256	                x: strip.maxX - padding - 6, y: strip.midY - 3, width: 6, height: 6)
257	            if dot.minX >= x {
258	                ClipLabel.color(named: label).withAlphaComponent(0.92).setFill()
259	                NSBezierPath(ovalIn: dot).fill()
260	                nameEnd = dot.minX - 5
261	                dotLeft = dot.minX
262	            }
263	        }
264	        // The during glyph: an 11 pt box (the kind icon's) at the right end,
265	        // 4 pt left of the label dot when one drew, guarded like the dot.
266	        if motion?.during != nil {
267	            let right = dotLeft.map { $0 - 4 } ?? (strip.maxX - padding)
268	            let glyph = CGRect(x: right - 11, y: strip.minY, width: 11, height: strip.height)
269	            if glyph.minX >= x {
270	                TimelineDraw.symbol(
271	                    "waveform.path", fallback: "~", in: glyph,
272	                    tint: NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.62))
273	                nameEnd = glyph.minX - 5
274	            }
275	        }
276	        TimelineDraw.truncated(
277	            owner.snapshot.name(of: clip),
278	            in: CGRect(x: x, y: strip.minY, width: max(nameEnd - x, 0), height: strip.height),
279	            font: DS.sans(10, weight: .semibold),
280	            color: NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.92))
281	    }

283	    /// The in and out wedges along the strip's bottom edge: a triangle as
284	    /// long as the preset's duration at this zoom, rising to 4 pt at its
285	    /// inner end, so the ramp reads as "how far in the motion runs". Base
286	    /// props, because motion ignores actions. A tent simply overlaps — the
287	    /// core resolves it, and no tent arithmetic belongs here.
288	    private func drawMotionWedges(
289	        _ motion: MotionProps, clip: ClipSnapshot, strip: CGRect, body: CGRect
290	    ) {
291	        let perTick = body.width / CGFloat(max(clip.duration, 1))
292	        // 2 pt minimum so a short preset still shows; never wider than the clip.
293	        func width(_ edge: MotionEdge) -> CGFloat {
294	            min(max(CGFloat(edge.duration) * perTick, 2), body.width)
295	        }
296	        // 0.55 white: a strip literal, a shade under the icon's 0.62.
297	        NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.55).setFill()
298	        if let edge = motion.inEdge, edge.isActive {
299	            let w = width(edge)
300	            let path = NSBezierPath()
301	            path.move(to: CGPoint(x: strip.minX, y: strip.maxY))
302	            path.line(to: CGPoint(x: strip.minX + w, y: strip.maxY))
303	            path.line(to: CGPoint(x: strip.minX + w, y: strip.maxY - 4))
304	            path.close()
305	            path.fill()
306	        }
307	        if let edge = motion.out, edge.isActive {
308	            let w = width(edge)
309	            let path = NSBezierPath()
310	            path.move(to: CGPoint(x: strip.maxX, y: strip.maxY))
311	            path.line(to: CGPoint(x: strip.maxX - w, y: strip.maxY))
312	            path.line(to: CGPoint(x: strip.maxX - w, y: strip.maxY - 4))
313	            path.close()
314	            path.fill()
315	        }
316	    }

318	    // There is deliberately NO second line under the name strip for a text or
319	    // shape clip. The design's mock shows one ("Title card" over "Nightfall"),
320	    // but a clip's own `name` (format version 3) is optional and most have
321	    // none: `ProjectSnapshot.name(of:)` then falls back to `clip.fallbackName`,
322	    // which for a text clip IS the text and for a shape clip IS the kind's
323	    // display name. Drawing it again under the strip made every text clip
324	    // stutter its own content. The strip carries whichever name the clip has.

326	    // MARK: - Transition
327	
328	    /// The overlap with the previous clip, drawn above both bars and so
329	    /// outside the body's clip. 45° hatch on the design's 3 pt line and 7 pt
330	    /// period (`hatchSpacing` below explains the √2) with a solid edge down
331	    /// each side, which is what makes the zone read as a span rather than as
332	    /// texture.
333	    ///
334	    /// `TimelineDraw.hatch` gained a defaulted line width for this — the
335	    /// locked-track hatch that shares it keeps its hairline — but it draws no
336	    /// edges, so those two are here.
337	    private func drawTransition(
338	        _ clip: ClipSnapshot, previous: ClipSnapshot?, in body: CGRect, layout: TimelineLayout
339	    ) {
340	        guard let transition = clip.transitionIn, let previous = previous,
341	              previous.end > clip.start
342	        else { return }
343	        let zone = CGRect(
344	            x: layout.x(for: clip.start), y: body.minY,
345	            width: max(layout.width(of: previous.end - clip.start), 2), height: body.height)
346	        TimelineDraw.hatch(
347	            zone, color: NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.26), spacing: Self.hatchSpacing,
348	            lineWidth: 3)
349	        NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.4).setFill()
350	        NSRect(x: zone.minX, y: zone.minY, width: 1, height: zone.height).fill()
351	        NSRect(x: zone.maxX - 1, y: zone.minY, width: 1, height: zone.height).fill()
352	
353	        // The kind is drawn only when the whole word fits between the two
354	        // edges with a little air. `TimelineDraw.label` CLIPS, so a 0.48 s
355	        // cross dissolve used to read "s Diss" — a middle of a word, which
356	        // says less than nothing. The Transition section of the inspector
357	        // names the kind, so a zone too short to hold it loses no information.
358	        let font = DS.sans(9)
359	        let name = transition.kind.displayName
360	        let width = name.size(withAttributes: [.font: font]).width
361	        guard width + 8 <= zone.width else { return }
362	        TimelineDraw.label(
363	            name,
364	            in: CGRect(x: zone.minX, y: zone.maxY - 13, width: zone.width, height: 12),
365	            font: font, color: NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.85), centered: true)
366	    }

368	    /// The hatch spacing that gives the design's 7 pt PERPENDICULAR period.
369	    ///
370	    /// `TimelineDraw.hatch` steps each line's origin along X while drawing at
371	    /// 45°, so the gap measured across the lines is `spacing / √2` — passing
372	    /// the design's 7 straight through gave a 4.95 pt period, and a 3 pt line
373	    /// on that is 61 % coverage where the design asks for 43 %. The scaling
374	    /// lives at THIS call site rather than in `hatch`, because the locked-track
375	    /// hatch shares that helper and its hairline lattice is what it should be.
376	    private static let hatchSpacing: CGFloat = 7 * 2.0.squareRoot()
377	
378	    // MARK: - Media
379	
380	    /// Thumbnails at the design's fixed 34 pt tile, then the clip's tint
381	    /// washed back over them at 54 %.
382	    ///
383	    /// The tile used to be the region's aspect-derived width, which made the
384	    /// strip's rhythm depend on the lane height; a fixed tile means the image
385	    /// no longer fits the box, so each one is drawn to FILL 34 pt and cropped
386	    /// rather than letterboxed.
387	    func drawFilmstrip(
388	        _ clip: ClipSnapshot, in rect: CGRect, tint: NSColor, owner: TimelineView, visible: CGRect
389	    ) {
390	        guard rect.height >= 10, rect.width > 0 else { return }
391	        if let directory = owner.cacheDirectory, let media = owner.snapshot.media(for: clip),
392	           media.width > 0, media.height > 0 {
393	            let tile = DS.filmstripThumb
394	            let skipped = max(((visible.minX - rect.minX) / tile).rounded(.down), 0)
395	            var x = rect.minX + skipped * tile
396	            let limit = min(rect.maxX, visible.maxX)
397	            NSGraphicsContext.current?.saveGraphicsState()
398	            NSBezierPath(rect: rect).addClip()
399	            NSGraphicsContext.current?.cgContext.setAlpha(0.72)
400	            let map = owner.sourceMaps(clip.id)
401	            while x < limit {
402	                let time = max(owner.layout.time(atX: x + tile / 2), clip.start)
403	                let source = TimelineView.sourceTime(of: clip, in: media, at: time, map: map)
404	                let index = Int(max(source, 0) / ReelTime.perSecond)
405	                let image = owner.caches.thumbnail(
406	                    media: media.id, index: index, in: directory)
407	                if let image = image {
408	                    Self.fill(
409	                        image, in: CGRect(x: x, y: rect.minY, width: tile, height: rect.height))
410	                }
411	                x += tile
412	            }
413	            NSGraphicsContext.current?.restoreGraphicsState()
414	        }
415	        tint.withAlphaComponent(0.54).setFill()
416	        rect.fill()
417	    }
418	
419	    /// A thumbnail scaled to COVER `rect` and cropped to it, which is what a
420	    /// fixed tile width needs — `TimelineDraw.image` stretches to fit and
421	    /// would squash every frame at the small lane sizes.
422	    private static func fill(_ image: CGImage, in rect: CGRect) {
423	        let width = CGFloat(image.width)
424	        let height = CGFloat(image.height)
425	        guard width > 0, height > 0, rect.width > 0, rect.height > 0 else { return }
426	        let scale = max(rect.width / width, rect.height / height)
427	        let target = CGRect(
428	            x: rect.midX - width * scale / 2, y: rect.midY - height * scale / 2,
429	            width: width * scale, height: height * scale)
430	        NSGraphicsContext.current?.saveGraphicsState()
431	        NSBezierPath(rect: rect).addClip()
432	        TimelineDraw.image(image, in: target)
433	        NSGraphicsContext.current?.restoreGraphicsState()
434	    }
435	
436	    /// The cached peaks (100 buckets per source second) as a column plot,
437	    /// symmetric about the REGION's centre line and filled at 44 % white.
438	    /// Muted draws at 40 % of that (spec §4.4).
439	    func drawWaveform(
440	        _ clip: ClipSnapshot, in rect: CGRect, owner: TimelineView, visible: CGRect, muted: Bool
441	    ) {
442	        guard rect.height >= 8, let directory = owner.cacheDirectory,
443	              let media = owner.snapshot.media(for: clip),
444	              let peaks = owner.caches.peaks(media: media.id, in: directory), !peaks.isEmpty
445	        else { return }
446	        let alpha: CGFloat = muted ? 0.4 : 1
447	        NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.44 * alpha).setFill()
448	        let midY = rect.midY
449	        let half = rect.height / 2 - 1
450	        let from = max(rect.minX, visible.minX)
451	        let to = min(rect.maxX, visible.maxX)
452	        var x = from.rounded(.down)
453	        let bucketsPerSecond = Double(MediaImporter.peakBucketsPerSecond)
454	        let map = owner.sourceMaps(clip.id)
455	        while x < to {
456	            let time = max(owner.layout.time(atX: x), clip.start)
457	            let source = TimelineView.sourceTime(of: clip, in: media, at: time, map: map)
458	            let bucket = Int(
459	                (Double(max(source, 0)) / Double(ReelTime.perSecond) * bucketsPerSecond)
460	                    .rounded(.down))
461	            guard peaks.indices.contains(bucket) else {
462	                x += 1
463	                continue
464	            }
465	            let amplitude = CGFloat(min(max(peaks[bucket], 0), 1)) * half
466	            NSRect(x: x, y: midY - amplitude, width: 1, height: max(amplitude * 2, 1)).fill()
467	            x += 1
468	        }
469	    }
470	}

472	// MARK: - Truncating label
473	
474	extension TimelineDraw {
475	    /// A one-line label that ends in an ellipsis instead of being cut off.
476	    ///
477	    /// `TimelineDraw.label` clips, which is right for a ruler tick that either
478	    /// fits or does not; a clip name has to say "there is more" — a strip
479	    /// reading "IMG_96" and one reading "IMG_96…" are different claims. Text
480	    /// is centred vertically in `rect` so a call site can pass the strip's
481	    /// whole height.
482	    static func truncated(_ text: String, in rect: CGRect, font: NSFont, color: NSColor) {
483	        guard rect.width > 4, rect.height > 4, !text.isEmpty else { return }
484	        let style = NSMutableParagraphStyle()
485	        style.lineBreakMode = .byTruncatingTail
486	        let attributes: [NSAttributedString.Key: Any] = [
487	            .font: font, .foregroundColor: color, .paragraphStyle: style,
488	        ]
489	        // The box is the LINE's natural height, centred on `rect`, never
490	        // `rect` itself: `draw(in:)` drops a line that does not fit its box
491	        // outright, so clamping the height to a 13 pt strip would silently
492	        // lose the name instead of shortening it.
493	        let height = ceil(text.size(withAttributes: attributes).height)
494	        text.draw(
495	            in: CGRect(
496	                x: rect.minX, y: (rect.midY - height / 2).rounded(), width: rect.width,
497	                height: height),
498	            withAttributes: attributes)
499	    }
500	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

## Reading a clip

Each clip is drawn as one rounded block with a thin border, so you can see
where one ends and the next begins.

- **Colour by kind**: video slate, audio green, image or still violet, text
  amber, shape teal (graphics use the same colour), nest grey, adjustment
  rose.
- **Name strip** along the top: a symbol for the kind, then the clip's name.
  A clip with no name of its own shows what it holds: its file, its text, its
  shape or its nest.
- **Label dot**: a labelled clip gets a small dot in its label colour at the
  right end of the name strip. The block's colour still shows its kind.
- **Filmstrip**: thumbnails along the picture part of a video or image clip,
  under a wash of the clip's colour. Each thumbnail is the source frame at
  that point, following speed, reverse and speed ramps.
- **Waveform**: the sound of a clip that has audio, drawn below the
  filmstrip on a clip that has both. Muted, or silenced by another track's
  solo, it draws faded.
- **Fade handles**: small white squares at the top corners of the audio part.
  Drag one inward to fade (see [Audio](audio.md)).
- **Volume line**: a thin white line over the waveform showing the level you
  hear from the clip, with small squares where a volume action ends. Drag it
  to change the level, or ⌥-click it to add a point (see
  [Audio](audio.md#the-volume-line)). A silenced clip's line lies along the
  bottom.
- **Motion marks**: small wedges at the ends of the name strip for an active
  In or Out motion, and a wave glyph for a During motion (see
  [Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md)).
- **Transitions**: the overlap between two clips is hatched, with the
  transition's kind written in it when the word fits.
- **Selected**: a 2 pt coral ring, with trim grips at both ends when the clip
  is wide enough to trim and its track is unlocked.
- **Linked**: a picture and the sound Detach Audio split from it each show a
  link symbol after the kind symbol. When one is selected, the other gets a
  dashed accent ring, because edits to one move both (see
  [Audio](audio.md#what-stays-in-sync)).
- **Dimmed**: a clip on a hidden track, or one with both its picture and its
  sound switched off.
- **No filmstrip**: text, shape, graphic, nest and adjustment clips have no
  thumbnails. An adjustment clip is a plain rose block with only its name
  strip and action lane, and its track is sized as a picture track.

Filmstrips and waveforms come from a cache made for each media file after
import, so they fill in a moment after a file is added.

### The action lane

A clip that has actions (keyframed segments) gets an **action lane** right
under its name strip. Each action is a band. At Medium and Large each band
shows its number in time order (and a zoom glyph for a zoom action); at Large
it also lists the properties it changes; at Small the bands are plain bars.
The selected action is solid, its span is washed down the clip, and it is
shaded on the ruler.

Hover a band to highlight it and show its 5 pt grips at both ends (a band
15 pt wide or less has none). The pointer is an open hand over the body and
a resize arrow over a grip.

Click a band to select the clip and that action; the playhead also moves to
the action's end, so the preview shows its end state. Drag a band's body to
move the action, or drag a grip to resize it. After a move or resize the
action stays selected and the playhead goes to its new end. When exactly one
clip is selected, playing or scrubbing into one of its actions' spans
selects that action. Esc leaves it, and ⌫ removes it.
Everything else about actions is on
[Motion and transitions](motion-and-transitions.md).

## The ruler and the playhead

The ruler's ticks adjust to the zoom, from single frames up to minutes.
Labels drop the hours when the timeline is under an hour long. The playhead
is the coral line with a triangle head on the ruler.

- **Click the ruler** to move the playhead there, and **drag** along it to
  scrub. Playback stops while you scrub, and you hear the sound under the
  playhead instead (see [Hearing a scrub](audio.md#hearing-a-scrub)). The
  scrub snaps like any other drag
  (see [Snapping](#snapping)).

3	/// One clip, drawn as ONE OBJECT (the redesign's §3).
4	///
5	/// The old bar had no boundary: the filmstrip and the waveform ran edge to
6	/// edge as two stacked bands and the name sat in a black strip that read as
7	/// part of the image, so you could not see where one clip ended and the next
8	/// began. What replaces it is a body — inset 3 pt from the lane, rounded,
9	/// clipped, with a 1 pt light border — carrying a 16 pt name strip along its
10	/// top and the media UNDER a wash of the clip's own tint, so a filmstrip reads
11	/// as a tinted clip rather than as a strip of photographs.
12	///
13	/// The alpha washes here are white-over-tint and black-over-tint literals
14	/// (0.14 border, 0.26 strip, 0.44 waveform, 0.54 wash, 0.62/0.72/0.92 inks).
15	/// They are deliberately NOT `DS` tokens: each is relative to the clip tint
16	/// underneath it, which is a fixed ink in both appearances, so a semantic
17	/// colour would break the contrast the design chose.
18	///
19	/// This is an extension of `TimelineContentView` — `TimelineView.swift` is
20	/// frozen at wiring (app/CLAUDE.md) and this is where the redesign's work
21	/// went.

23	    /// The clip's body: the lane rect inset 3 pt top and bottom, which is the
24	    /// gap that makes two lanes read as two rows of objects.
25	    static func bodyRect(_ rect: CGRect) -> CGRect {
26	        CGRect(
27	            x: rect.minX, y: rect.minY + 3, width: rect.width,
28	            height: max(rect.height - 6, 1))
29	    }

32	    /// the fade handles live.

35	    /// fade handle at the audio region's corner): the handles moved down by
36	    /// the strip's height when the body arrived, and a hit test still measuring
37	    /// from the lane's top edge would leave them undraggable.
38	    static func contentRect(_ rect: CGRect) -> CGRect {
39	        let body = bodyRect(rect)

41	            x: body.minX, y: body.minY + DS.clipHeaderHeight, width: body.width,

47	    /// lies inside the PREVIOUS clip's body, over its right edge: drawn with
48	    /// that clip, the NEXT clip's hatch painted white 0.26 and a solid white
49	    /// edge straight over the previous clip's ring (#66). Clips outside
50	    /// `dirtyRect` are skipped in every pass. On a matte track the first two
51	    /// passes run at half opacity inside `drawMatteLane` (spec §11 MT-7,
52	    /// `TimelineView+Matte.swift`); the rings stay whole.
53	    func drawClips(
54	        _ clips: [ClipSnapshot], row: Int, track: TrackSnapshot, owner: TimelineView,
55	        dirtyRect: CGRect
56	    ) {
57	        let rects = clips.map { owner.layout.clipRect($0, row: row) }
58	        let shown = clips.indices.filter { rects[$0].intersects(dirtyRect) }
59	        drawMatteLane(
60	            track: track, rects: shown.map { rects[$0] },
61	            lane: owner.layout.rowRect(row, width: owner.layout.contentWidth), owner: owner
62	        ) {
63	            for i in shown {
64	                draw(clip: clips[i], in: rects[i], track: track, owner: owner, visible: dirtyRect)
65	            }
66	            for i in shown where i > 0 {
67	                drawTransition(
68	                    clips[i], previous: clips[i - 1], in: Self.bodyRect(rects[i]),
69	                    layout: owner.layout)

73	            drawSelectionRing(Self.bodyRect(rects[i]))

77	        // that is itself selected has its own ring.
78	        for i in shown {

297	        NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.55).setFill()
298	        if let edge = motion.inEdge, edge.isActive {
299	            let w = width(edge)
300	            let path = NSBezierPath()

302	            path.line(to: CGPoint(x: strip.minX + w, y: strip.maxY))
303	            path.line(to: CGPoint(x: strip.minX + w, y: strip.maxY - 4))

306	        }
307	        if let edge = motion.out, edge.isActive {
308	            let w = width(edge)

310	            path.move(to: CGPoint(x: strip.maxX, y: strip.maxY))
311	            path.line(to: CGPoint(x: strip.maxX - w, y: strip.maxY))

351	        NSRect(x: zone.maxX - 1, y: zone.minY, width: 1, height: zone.height).fill()
352	
353	        // The kind is drawn only when the whole word fits between the two
354	        // edges with a little air. `TimelineDraw.label` CLIPS, so a 0.48 s
355	        // cross dissolve used to read "s Diss" — a middle of a word, which
356	        // says less than nothing. The Transition section of the inspector
357	        // names the kind, so a zone too short to hold it loses no information.
358	        let font = DS.sans(9)
359	        let name = transition.kind.displayName
360	        let width = name.size(withAttributes: [.font: font]).width
361	        guard width + 8 <= zone.width else { return }
362	        TimelineDraw.label(
363	            name,
364	            in: CGRect(x: zone.minX, y: zone.maxY - 13, width: zone.width, height: 12),
365	            font: font, color: NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.85), centered: true)
366	    }
367	
368	    /// The hatch spacing that gives the design's 7 pt PERPENDICULAR period.
369	    ///
370	    /// `TimelineDraw.hatch` steps each line's origin along X while drawing at
371	    /// 45°, so the gap measured across the lines is `spacing / √2` — passing
372	    /// the design's 7 straight through gave a 4.95 pt period, and a 3 pt line
373	    /// on that is 61 % coverage where the design asks for 43 %. The scaling
374	    /// lives at THIS call site rather than in `hatch`, because the locked-track
375	    /// hatch shares that helper and its hairline lattice is what it should be.
376	    private static let hatchSpacing: CGFloat = 7 * 2.0.squareRoot()
377	
378	    // MARK: - Media
379	
380	    /// Thumbnails at the design's fixed 34 pt tile, then the clip's tint
381	    /// washed back over them at 54 %.
382	    ///
383	    /// The tile used to be the region's aspect-derived width, which made the
384	    /// strip's rhythm depend on the lane height; a fixed tile means the image
385	    /// no longer fits the box, so each one is drawn to FILL 34 pt and cropped
386	    /// rather than letterboxed.
387	    func drawFilmstrip(
388	        _ clip: ClipSnapshot, in rect: CGRect, tint: NSColor, owner: TimelineView, visible: CGRect
389	    ) {
390	        guard rect.height >= 10, rect.width > 0 else { return }
391	        if let directory = owner.cacheDirectory, let media = owner.snapshot.media(for: clip),
392	           media.width > 0, media.height > 0 {
393	            let tile = DS.filmstripThumb
394	            let skipped = max(((visible.minX - rect.minX) / tile).rounded(.down), 0)
395	            var x = rect.minX + skipped * tile
396	            let limit = min(rect.maxX, visible.maxX)
397	            NSGraphicsContext.current?.saveGraphicsState()
398	            NSBezierPath(rect: rect).addClip()
399	            NSGraphicsContext.current?.cgContext.setAlpha(0.72)
400	            let map = owner.sourceMaps(clip.id)
401	            while x < limit {
402	                let time = max(owner.layout.time(atX: x + tile / 2), clip.start)
403	                let source = TimelineView.sourceTime(of: clip, in: media, at: time, map: map)
404	                let index = Int(max(source, 0) / ReelTime.perSecond)
405	                let image = owner.caches.thumbnail(
406	                    media: media.id, index: index, in: directory)
407	                if let image = image {
408	                    Self.fill(
409	                        image, in: CGRect(x: x, y: rect.minY, width: tile, height: rect.height))
410	                }
411	                x += tile
412	            }
413	            NSGraphicsContext.current?.restoreGraphicsState()
414	        }
415	        tint.withAlphaComponent(0.54).setFill()
416	        rect.fill()
417	    }
418	
419	    /// A thumbnail scaled to COVER `rect` and cropped to it, which is what a
420	    /// fixed tile width needs — `TimelineDraw.image` stretches to fit and
421	    /// would squash every frame at the small lane sizes.
422	    private static func fill(_ image: CGImage, in rect: CGRect) {
423	        let width = CGFloat(image.width)
424	        let height = CGFloat(image.height)
425	        guard width > 0, height > 0, rect.width > 0, rect.height > 0 else { return }
426	        let scale = max(rect.width / width, rect.height / height)
427	        let target = CGRect(
428	            x: rect.midX - width * scale / 2, y: rect.midY - height * scale / 2,
429	            width: width * scale, height: height * scale)
430	        NSGraphicsContext.current?.saveGraphicsState()
431	        NSBezierPath(rect: rect).addClip()
432	        TimelineDraw.image(image, in: target)
433	        NSGraphicsContext.current?.restoreGraphicsState()
434	    }
435	
436	    /// The cached peaks (100 buckets per source second) as a column plot,
437	    /// symmetric about the REGION's centre line and filled at 44 % white.
438	    /// Muted draws at 40 % of that (spec §4.4).
439	    func drawWaveform(
440	        _ clip: ClipSnapshot, in rect: CGRect, owner: TimelineView, visible: CGRect, muted: Bool
441	    ) {
442	        guard rect.height >= 8, let directory = owner.cacheDirectory,
443	              let media = owner.snapshot.media(for: clip),
444	              let peaks = owner.caches.peaks(media: media.id, in: directory), !peaks.isEmpty
445	        else { return }
446	        let alpha: CGFloat = muted ? 0.4 : 1
447	        NSColor.white.withAlphaComponent(0.44 * alpha).setFill()
448	        let midY = rect.midY
449	        let half = rect.height / 2 - 1
450	        let from = max(rect.minX, visible.minX)
451	        let to = min(rect.maxX, visible.maxX)
452	        var x = from.rounded(.down)
453	        let bucketsPerSecond = Double(MediaImporter.peakBucketsPerSecond)
454	        let map = owner.sourceMaps(clip.id)
455	        while x < to {
456	            let time = max(owner.layout.time(atX: x), clip.start)
457	            let source = TimelineView.sourceTime(of: clip, in: media, at: time, map: map)
458	            let bucket = Int(
459	                (Double(max(source, 0)) / Double(ReelTime.perSecond) * bucketsPerSecond)
460	                    .rounded(.down))
461	            guard peaks.indices.contains(bucket) else {
462	                x += 1
463	                continue
464	            }
465	            let amplitude = CGFloat(min(max(peaks[bucket], 0), 1)) * half
466	            NSRect(x: x, y: midY - amplitude, width: 1, height: max(amplitude * 2, 1)).fill()
467	            x += 1
468	        }
469	    }
470	}
471	
472	// MARK: - Truncating label
473	
474	extension TimelineDraw {
475	    /// A one-line label that ends in an ellipsis instead of being cut off.
476	    ///
477	    /// `TimelineDraw.label` clips, which is right for a ruler tick that either
478	    /// fits or does not; a clip name has to say "there is more" — a strip
479	    /// reading "IMG_96" and one reading "IMG_96…" are different claims. Text
480	    /// is centred vertically in `rect` so a call site can pass the strip's
481	    /// whole height.
482	    static func truncated(_ text: String, in rect: CGRect, font: NSFont, color: NSColor) {
483	        guard rect.width > 4, rect.height > 4, !text.isEmpty else { return }
484	        let style = NSMutableParagraphStyle()
485	        style.lineBreakMode = .byTruncatingTail
486	        let attributes: [NSAttributedString.Key: Any] = [
487	            .font: font, .foregroundColor: color, .paragraphStyle: style,
488	        ]
489	        // The box is the LINE's natural height, centred on `rect`, never
490	        // `rect` itself: `draw(in:)` drops a line that does not fit its box
491	        // outright, so clamping the height to a 13 pt strip would silently
492	        // lose the name instead of shortening it.
493	        let height = ceil(text.size(withAttributes: attributes).height)
494	        text.draw(
495	            in: CGRect(
496	                x: rect.minX, y: (rect.midY - height / 2).rounded(), width: rect.width,
497	                height: height),
498	            withAttributes: attributes)
499	    }
500	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `VideoProps.swift` · `ClipSnapshot.swift` ·
  `TrackSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` · `CursorProps.swift` · `CutoutProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading GR1) is the plan's Swift side (spec §7.2): `PlanSegment`,
  `PlanRamp`, `PlanTrack`, `PlanInstruction` and `CompositionPlan`; `PlanSpeedRamp.source` is
  its `map` as a `SourceMap`, checked once at decode and not a coding key (SR-20 (c));
  `PlanSegment.path` (the clip alone when absent) and `origin` (nil) read a nested audio
  segment's instance (spec §11 TX-10); `PlanDuck`
  and `ducks` are a speech ducker's own multiplier (format 29, spec §11 AU-113); `PlanGate` and
  `gates` a gated clip's hide-while-silent gate (format 43, spec §11 CO-93). `AudioProps.swift`
  (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, road map "audio" AP11's toll) holds the audio group:
  `AudioProps`, `DuckProps` and `CompressorProps`, with format 29's `DuckMode`,
  `DuckProps.mode` / `preRoll` / `hold` and `FadeShape` (and the popups' titles), and format
  30's `LimiterProps` (`audio.limiter`, spec §11 AU-21) with its patch body,
  and format 31's `AudioProps.isolation` (AU-50), and format 32's `eq`, `hum` and `channels`
  (`AudioEQProps.swift`, AU-31, AU-33, AU-34), and format 33's `gate` and `deEsser`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-43, AU-45), and format 34's `voice`
  (`VoiceProps.swift`, AU-140), and format 37's `leveller`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-66);
  `ClipSnapshot.swift`'s `TransitionSnapshot.audioShape` is `plus_3db` when absent, and
  `MediaSnapshot.speech` the media's saved spans. `CursorProps.swift` (format 38, road map
  creator-jobs CU3a1, spec §11 CU-30, CU-39) holds `CursorStyle`, `CursorClicks` (`off` is the
  core's `none`: a case named `none` warns), `CursorProps` (`VideoProps.cursor` and
  `VideoPatch.cursor`; its `dictionary` writes all eight keys, `NSNull` for a nil `hideIdle`),
  `CursorPatch` (all eight keys, the sparse write `VideoPatch.cursorPart` carries — written
  under `cursor` only when `cursor` is nil, never decoded, `cutoutPart`'s shape — so each Cursor
  row writes its own key alone, CU3b, CU4, spec §11 CU-38 (b), CU-40; `clipsOwn` (smoothing,
  hide_idle) and `animatable` (the other six)), with `CursorProps.smoothingSteps`,
  `hideIdleSteps` and `polished`,
  `MediaCursor` (`MediaSnapshot.cursor`, `MediaDescriptor.cursor`, kept by `probeDictionary`) and
  `RecipeCursor` (the recipe layer's `cursor`, `media` and `at` required).
  `CutoutProps.swift` (format 39, road map creator-jobs CO2a1, spec §11 CO-20, CO-21;
  `foreground` and the image arm format 41, CO10a, CO-100, CO-101) holds `CutoutSubject`
  (`person`, `foreground`), `CutoutQuality`, `CutoutBackground`, `CutoutProps` (`VideoProps.cutout` and
  `VideoPatch.cutout`; its `dictionary` writes all five keys), `CutoutPatch` (the sparse
  write `VideoPatch.cutoutPart` carries — written under `cutout` only when `cutout` is nil,
  never decoded — so a Background, Edge or Feather row writes its own key alone, CO3),
  `RecipeCutoutMaskKind` (`media`, and `image`, drawn since CO10b from the
  picture's one mask, CO-107),
  `RecipeCutoutMask` (`kind` and `media` required; `subject` lenient,
  `person` when absent, CO-101) and `RecipeCutout` (the recipe layer's
  `cutout`, `mask` required; `subjectCopy`, CO-51); `RecipeLayer.videoProps` passes no cutout — the recipe's is a draw
  instruction, not the clip's props. `VideoProps.swift` (`VideoProps`),
  `ClipSnapshot.swift` (`ClipSource` with its nested `CodingKeys`, `ClipSnapshot`,
  `TransitionSnapshot`) and `TrackSnapshot.swift` (`TrackSnapshot`) are pure moves out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T11–T13). `ShapeProps.swift` (a pure
  move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading L3) holds the shape group: `StrokeProps`,
  `GradientStop`, `Gradient` and `ShapeProps`. `GradeProps.swift` holds `ColorAdjust` (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) beside grading's other value types. `ActionSnapshot.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, B87) holds `ActionPatch`, `ActionSnapshot` and `ActionGraphicPatch` — an
  end's `graphic.props` and `kinds`, whose `dictionary` sends `props` only. `MediaSnapshot` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`) carries a copy's or an ffmpeg conversion's `original`, and its `name` is
  the one display-name spelling: the original's name when one is recorded. **Its enums decode LENIENTLY**
  — a misspelt kind becomes the first case, a `T??` field a clear — which is
  why a caller-authored object is never decoded through them (below). The
  one exception is `ClipSource`: an unknown `source.kind` THROWS, and
  `ReelProject.snapshot` then falls back to `.empty`, so the WHOLE project
  draws empty with no error. A new source kind in the core is therefore a
  `ClipSource` case in the same phase (road map 10's G2a added `graphic`): no

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

import AppKit

/// How a clip's KIND is spelled in the chrome: its tint, its symbol and the
/// one word that names it.
///
/// Four places show the same chip — the timeline clip's name strip, the
/// timeline bar's selection block, the inspector's selection header and the
/// Media tab — and they must agree, so the mapping lives here rather than four
/// times over. It is spec §4.4's table ("video slate, audio green, still
/// violet, text amber, shape teal, nest grey"), moved out of `TimelineView`
/// now that three views other than the timeline read it.
///
/// **Every entry point takes the snapshot**, and that is the one substantive
/// change to the old mapping. It used to answer for a `media` clip from
/// `clip.enabled.video` alone, which is the DETACH switch, not a fact about
/// the file: an imported mp3 has `enabled.video == true` (nothing ever turned
/// it off) and so drew slate blue with a filmstrip icon and called itself
/// "video" in two selection blocks. Only the media entry knows whether there
/// are pixels, so the tests are `media.hasVideo` and `media.hasAudio`, exactly
/// as `TimelineView.hasVideo` / `hasAudio` ask them — a clip reads as audio
/// when it has no picture to show, whether that is because the file has none
/// or because Detach Audio took it away.
enum ClipKindStyle {
    /// The kinds the chrome distinguishes. Not `ClipSource`'s cases: `media`
    /// splits by what the file actually holds, and `still` and `image` share
    /// one ink because both are a picture that does not move.
    enum Kind {
        case video
        case audio
        case still
        case text
        case shape
        case graphic
        case nest
        case adjustment
    }

    static func kind(of clip: ClipSnapshot, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> Kind {
        switch clip.source {
        case .media:
            let hasPicture = clip.enabled.video && (snapshot.media(for: clip)?.hasVideo ?? false)
            return hasPicture ? .video : .audio
        case .still, .image:
            return .still
        case .text:
            return .text
        case .shape:
            return .shape
        case .graphic:
            return .graphic
        case .nest:
            return .nest
        case .adjustment:
            return .adjustment
        }
    }

    /// The clip tint of spec §4.4, from `Theme.swift`'s tokens.
    static func tint(for clip: ClipSnapshot, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> NSColor {
        switch kind(of: clip, in: snapshot) {
        case .video: return DS.clipVideo
        case .audio: return DS.clipAudio
        case .still: return DS.clipStill
        case .text: return DS.clipText
        case .shape: return DS.clipShape
        // Shape's ink until road map 10's G5 gives a graphic a token.
        case .graphic: return DS.clipShape
        case .nest: return DS.clipNest
        case .adjustment: return DS.clipAdjustment
        }
    }

    /// The SF Symbol for a clip's kind, with the glyph to fall back to when
    /// the symbol is missing (the `GhostButton` rule).
    static func symbol(
        for clip: ClipSnapshot, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot
    ) -> (name: String, fallback: String) {
        switch kind(of: clip, in: snapshot) {
        case .video: return ("film", "▦")
        case .audio: return ("waveform", "∿")
        case .still:
            if case .still = clip.source { return ("snowflake", "❄") }
            return ("photo", "▣")
        case .text: return ("textformat", "T")
        case .shape: return ("square.on.circle", "▭")
        case .graphic: return ("curlybraces", "{}")
        case .nest: return ("square.stack.3d.down.right", "▤")
        case .adjustment: return ("camera.filters", "◐")
        }
    }

    /// The lowercase word under a clip's name in a selection block.
    static func name(for clip: ClipSnapshot, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> String {
        switch kind(of: clip, in: snapshot) {
        case .video: return "video"
        case .audio: return "audio"
        case .still:
            if case .still = clip.source { return "still" }
            return "image"
        case .text: return "text"
        case .shape: return "shape"
        case .graphic: return "graphic"
        case .nest: return "nest"
        case .adjustment: return "adjustment"
        }
    }
}

## Playback

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| Space | Play / pause |
| J | Play backwards; press again for 2×, then 4× |
| K | Pause |
| L | Play forwards; press again for 2×, then 4× |
| ← / → | Back / forward one frame (pauses) |
| ⇧← / ⇧→ | Back / forward ten frames |
| ↑ / ↓ | Previous / next edit point |
| Home / End | Go to the start / end |

**Edit points** are the start and end of the timeline and the start and end
of every clip. ↑ with nothing earlier goes to the start.

J pressed while playing forwards, or L while playing backwards, switches
direction at 1×.

Space plays and pauses wherever the focus is, except while you type in a
text field or when a focused button uses the key itself. Typing ends with
Return, Tab or a click outside the field (on the timeline, say), and Space
plays straight after it. On the preview
canvas a quick Space press still plays or pauses (when you let go), while
holding Space and dragging pans the canvas instead. Holding Space down
doesn't toggle playback over and over. Letter keys never
fire while you are typing in a field, and no editor key works while a sheet
is open.

Playback stops at the end of the timeline. An empty timeline has nothing to
play: Play beeps.

### Loop

Turn on **Loop** in the toolbar to loop playback. With an in/out range set it
loops the range; otherwise it loops the whole timeline. Pressing play at or
past the end of the loop starts again from the loop's start. Loop is set per
window and isn't saved.

### What you'll notice after an edit

- A change that only alters how something looks (a property, a colour, text)
  redraws the frame in place without interrupting playback.
- A change to the timeline's structure (a move, a trim, a new clip) rebuilds
  the player in the background. It keeps your place and keeps playing at the
  same rate. While you drag, the rebuild waits until you pause briefly.
- If a rebuild fails, an error is shown and the previous version keeps
  playing.

*Agents:* `set_playhead {t}` moves the playhead and seeks the preview.
`get_project` reports the playhead, selection and in/out range along with the
project. `render_frame` writes the frame at a time as a PNG.

## Zooming the timeline
## The ruler and the playhead

The ruler's ticks adjust to the zoom, from single frames up to minutes.
Labels drop the hours when the timeline is under an hour long. The playhead
is the coral line with a triangle head on the ruler.

- **Click the ruler** to move the playhead there, and **drag** along it to
  scrub. Playback stops while you scrub, and you hear the sound under the
  playhead instead (see [Hearing a scrub](audio.md#hearing-a-scrub)). The
  scrub snaps like any other drag
  (see [Snapping](#snapping)).
- The timeline scrolls itself to keep the playhead in view: when the playhead
  leaves the visible part, during playback or after a jump, the view moves
  so the playhead sits about a third of the way in.
- A click in a lane doesn't move the playhead. It starts a marquee selection
  (see [Selecting clips](#selecting-clips)).

The editor with a small project in it and nothing selected: this is the screen
a person spends most of their time in, watching the preview while arranging clips
on the timeline.

The toolbar shows the playhead at "00:00:02:15" of "00:00:05:07". The preview
shows the frame under the playhead: a navy video frame, the white word "Frame Job"
inside a white ellipse outline over it, and a lower-third title in the bottom left
— a dark box with an orange bar at its left edge, "Jane Doe" in bold and "Director
of Photography" beneath. The inspector reads "Select a clip to edit its
properties." because nothing is selected.

The timeline shows four tracks, each a named row with the eye, speaker, lock and
headphone icons: Music, holding a green audio clip "toneA.m4a" with a pale level
line across it, its waveform band, and over that its volume line, a thin white
line across the clip at its level; Shapes, a teal clip "Ellipse"; Graphics, a taller teal clip "Graphic";
and Titles, an orange clip "Frame Job". Each clip's name sits in a darker strip
along its top with a small icon for its kind. The red playhead is at about the
2.5-second mark, a thin line through every track.

In the light capture the toolbar, the inspector and the track headers are white
