---
title: Reading a clip on the timeline
description: What every colour, symbol, line and handle on a clip block means, so you can read a timeline without selecting anything.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

A clip on the timeline tells you what it is, what it holds and what's been done to it, without being selected. This page is the key to those marks. Each mark's control has its own page, linked from here.

<AtAGlance where="The timeline's lanes" tools={['set_selection', 'set_audio']} />

<Shot
  name="04-editor.window"
  alt="The editor with four tracks on the timeline: a green audio clip with its waveform and a white volume line, two teal clips for a shape and a graphic, and an amber text clip. Each clip has its name in a darker strip along the top with a small symbol for its kind, and the playhead runs through every track."
/>

## The clip block

Each clip draws as one block with 2 pt rounded corners and a thin border, so you can always see where one clip ends and the next begins.

From top to bottom, a block holds its name strip, its action lane if it has actions, its filmstrip and its waveform. The filmstrip and the waveform sit under a wash of the clip's own colour, so a clip reads as one coloured object rather than a row of photographs.

The action lane shows a band for each [action](/motion/action-lane/). The selected action's span is also washed down the whole clip, in the action colour: mint in the dark look, a deeper green in the light one.

## Colour by kind

A clip's colour and the symbol on its name strip tell you its kind.

| Kind | Colour | Symbol |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Video | Slate | A strip of film |
| Audio | Green | A waveform |
| Image | Violet | A photo |
| Freeze frame | Violet | A snowflake |
| Text | Amber | Letters |
| Shape | Teal | A square on a circle |
| Graphic | Teal | Curly braces |
| Nest | Grey | A stack of squares |
| Adjustment | Rose | Overlapping filter circles |

The kind comes from what the clip shows, not only from its file. A video file's clip with its picture switched off reads as audio, in green with the waveform symbol. That's how the sound half of a [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) pair looks.

A [label](/timeline/names-and-labels/) never changes the block's colour, because the colour says what the clip is and a label is something you said about it.

## The name strip

The darker strip along the top of a clip carries, from left to right, its kind symbol, a link symbol if it's [linked](#linked-clips), its name, a wave if it has a During motion, and its label dot.

A clip with a name of its own shows that. Otherwise it shows what it holds: a nest's name, the file's name, the text itself, or the shape's kind. A clip with none of those reads as its kind, such as **Graphic** or **Adjustment**. A name too long for the strip ends in an ellipsis.

On a narrow clip the strip gives things up from the right. The kind symbol stays longest, and the dot and the wave are left out when they'd run into it.

### The label dot

A labelled clip shows a small dot in its label colour at the right end of the name strip. See [Clip names and labels](/timeline/names-and-labels/).

### Motion marks

Two small marks show a clip's active [motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/):

- **A wedge** along the bottom of the name strip, from the left end for an In preset and from the right end for an Out preset. It's as long as the preset's duration at the current zoom, and it rises towards its inner end, so you can see how far into the clip the motion runs. It's never shorter than 2 pt or wider than the clip.
- **A small wave** at the right end of the strip, just left of the label dot, for a During movement.

A detached sound half shows neither, even though it holds a copy of the picture's settings.

## Picture and sound

### Filmstrip

Thumbnails run along the picture part of a video, image or freeze frame clip, each 34 pt wide and cropped to fill its tile.

Each thumbnail is the source frame at that point in the clip, to the nearest earlier whole second of the source, and it follows the clip's trims, speed, reverse and speed ramps. A filmstrip of a log, PQ or HLG file shows the converted picture, not the flat image in the file.

Text, shape, graphic, nest and adjustment clips have no thumbnails.

### Waveform

A clip with sound draws it as a waveform, below the filmstrip when the clip has both. The waveform follows the clip's source time through speed changes and ramps.

The waveform draws faded when the clip or its track is muted, or when another track's solo silences it. A track's mute button stays unlit under another track's solo, so the waveform is the place to look to see what's in the mix. See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/) and [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/).

### Filling in after import

Filmstrips and waveforms are made once for each file and kept with the project, so they fill in a moment after you add a file. See [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/).

## Lines over a clip

Up to four thin lines show how a clip changes over time. All of them are read off the clip as it plays, and each has its own control.

### The volume line

A thin white line over the waveform shows the level you hear from the clip, with its volume, fades, ducking and volume actions folded in. The top of the audio part is +30 dB and the bottom is −60 dB, and a silenced clip's line lies along the bottom. Small squares in the action colour mark where a volume action ends.

Nest clips don't draw it. To change the level from the timeline, see [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/).

### The duck line

A thin yellow line over a clip set to duck by speech shows where the rest of the mix goes down and comes back. The top of the audio part is the mix at full level and the bottom is silence.

A duck set to **Clip Length** draws no line, because it lasts as long as the clip. See [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/).

### The Hide While Silent line

A teal line across the picture part of a clip with [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) on shows where the clip fades out in each pause and back in before speech. The top is fully shown and the bottom is fully hidden.

### The rate line

A clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) draws its rate as a white line with a dark edge across its action lane, here and in the Clip tab's lane. The bottom of the lane is the clip's own slowest rate and the top its fastest, so a small ramp looks as tall as a big one. Read the numbers in the Speed section.

The timeline draws it at the Medium and Large [track heights](/timeline/track-height/), not at Small.

## Fade handles

Small white squares at the top corners of a clip's audio part set its fades. Drag one inward to fade in or out. The square sits at the corner with no fade, and at the end of the fade once there is one.

The fade's length snaps to whole frames and stops at the clip's length. It doesn't snap to clip edges. The handles write the same two values as the Fades section, so see [Audio fades](/audio/fades/) for the rest.

## The transition zone

The overlap between two clips draws as a hatched zone with a solid edge down each side. The transition's kind is written in it when the whole word fits. On a short transition the word is left out, and the [Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/) still names it. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).

## Selected clips

A selected clip gets a 2 pt coral ring, and most commands act on it. When the clip is wide enough to trim and its track is unlocked, it also shows a trim grip at each end. See [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/).

## Linked clips

A picture and the sound Detach Audio split from it each show a link symbol after their kind symbol. Select one and the other gets a dashed ring in your Mac's accent colour, because edits to one move both. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).

## Dimmed clips

A clip draws dimmed when its track is hidden, or when both its picture and its sound are switched off. A muted clip isn't dimmed. Only its waveform fades.

## Adjustment clips

An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) is a plain rose block with only its name strip and action lane. It has no filmstrip or waveform, and its track is as tall as a picture track.

## Good to know

- A short track leaves marks out. The filmstrip needs 10 pt of height, the waveform, duck line and Hide While Silent line 8 pt, the fade handles 10 pt and the volume line 12 pt. A text clip at the Small [track height](/timeline/track-height/) is little more than its name strip.
- A [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) draws a faint hatch across its whole lane, over its clips. Clips on it show no trim grips.
- On a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), clips draw at half strength with a dashed outline.
- Inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/), a Hide While Silent line that reads its sound from outside the nest isn't drawn, though the clip still fades.

## Related

- [Clip names and labels](/timeline/names-and-labels/)
- [Track height](/timeline/track-height/)
- [Action bands and the action lane](/motion/action-lane/)

---
title: The ruler and playhead
description: Read the timeline's time ruler, scrub along it, and see how the playhead decides where edits land.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The ruler is the strip of time above the tracks. The playhead marks one moment on it: the frame the preview shows, and the point where most edits land.

<AtAGlance where="The ruler above the timeline's tracks" tools="set_playhead" />

## The playhead

The playhead is the coral line down every track, with a triangle head on the ruler. It always sits on a frame.

## Scrub on the ruler

Click the ruler to move the playhead there, and drag along it to scrub. Pressing on the ruler pauses playback, and it stays paused when you let go.

While you scrub, you hear the sound under the playhead. The press plays a short piece of it, and so does each new frame the drag reaches. See [Hear a scrub](/audio/scrub-audio/).

The scrub [snaps](/timeline/snapping/) like any other drag. Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> as you press to scrub without snapping.

A press within 6 pt of a marker's flag takes the [marker](/timeline/markers/), not the ruler, so start the scrub just beside it.

## Lane clicks

A click in a lane doesn't move the playhead. On empty space it starts a [marquee selection](/timeline/selecting-clips/), and a plain click there clears the selection.

## The edit point

These commands work at the playhead, so put it where you want the edit first:

| Command | Key |
| --- | --- |
| **Clip ▸ Split** | <kbd>⌘T</kbd> |
| **Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead** | <kbd>W</kbd> |
| **Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead** | <kbd>E</kbd> |
| **Clip ▸ Freeze Frame** | <kbd>⇧⌘F</kbd> |
| **Edit ▸ Paste** | <kbd>⌘V</kbd> |
| **Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead** | |
| **Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead** | |

To place the playhead exactly, [step by frames](/timeline/playback/#step-frames) or [jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/).

## Ticks and labels

The ruler's ticks adapt to the zoom. Zoomed in, they mark single frames. As you zoom out, they step through 2, 5 and 10 frames, then 1, 2, 5, 10, 15 and 30 seconds, then 1, 2, 5, 10, 15 and 30 minutes, and at the widest one hour.

Labels use the project's timecode format, **Frames** or **Milliseconds**, set in [the Document tab](/projects/background-and-timecode/). A timeline under an hour long drops the leading `00:` from its labels so they fit.

The ruler also carries [markers](/timeline/markers/), the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) and the selected [action's](/motion/action-lane/) span. Inside an open [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/), it counts from the nest's own start.

## Following the playhead

The timeline scrolls itself to keep the playhead in view, during playback and after a jump. When the playhead comes within 24 pt of either edge of the visible part, or leaves it, the view moves so the playhead sits about a third of the way in.

## With an agent

`set_playhead` moves the playhead and the preview, in silence. It isn't an edit, so there's nothing to undo. An agent that splits, freezes a frame or adds a marker without giving a time works at the playhead. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).

## Related

- [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/)
- [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/)
- [Zoom and scroll the timeline](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/)
- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)

---
title: Play, pause and shuttle
description: Play the timeline with Space, shuttle it at up to four times speed with J, K and L, and step it frame by frame.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Playback runs from the keyboard: <kbd>Space</kbd> to play and pause, <kbd>J</kbd>, <kbd>K</kbd> and <kbd>L</kbd> to shuttle, and the arrow keys to step to the frame you want.

<AtAGlance
  keys={['Space', 'J', 'K', 'L', '←', '→', '⇧←', '⇧→']}
  where="The Play and Pause button in the toolbar"
  tools="set_playhead"
/>

## Play and pause

Press <kbd>Space</kbd>, or the Play button in the toolbar's transport. The button shows Play or Pause to match, and it stays in the same spot. There's no menu item for it.

<kbd>Space</kbd> works from wherever the focus is in the window, with a few exceptions:

| Where you are | What <kbd>Space</kbd> does |
| --- | --- |
| Typing in a text field, the Text tab's text area, the canvas text editor or the Media tab's search field | Types a space. Typing ends with <kbd>Return</kbd>, <kbd>Tab</kbd> or a click outside the field, and <kbd>Space</kbd> plays straight after. |
| On the preview canvas | Plays or pauses when you let go, because the press gets ready to [pan](/canvas/zoom-and-pan/). If you panned while holding it, letting go does nothing. |
| On a button, pop-up or segmented control focused with Full Keyboard Access | Presses that control. |
| With a sheet open | Doesn't play or pause. |

<kbd>⇧Space</kbd> plays and pauses too. Any other modifier leaves the key alone. Holding <kbd>Space</kbd> down doesn't toggle playback over and over.

## J, K and L

<kbd>L</kbd> plays forward, <kbd>J</kbd> plays in reverse and <kbd>K</kbd> pauses.

| --- | --- |

- In the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-keys/), they move by word.

## At the end

Playback stops at the end of the timeline. With [Loop](/timeline/loop/) on, it goes back to the start of the loop instead.

## After an edit

You can edit while the timeline plays. What you notice depends on what you changed.

A change that only alters how something looks, such as a clip's position, a colour or some text, redraws the frame in place. Playback isn't interrupted.

### Structural edits

A move, a trim, a new clip or anything else that changes the timeline's shape rebuilds the player in the background. So does a change to the sound, such as volume, pan or the compressor. Frame Job keeps your place and keeps playing at the same rate. While you drag, the rebuild waits until you pause briefly.

If a rebuild fails, Frame Job shows the error and the previous version keeps playing.

---
title: Reading a clip on the timeline
description: What every colour, symbol, line and handle on a clip block means, so you can read a timeline without selecting anything.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

A clip on the timeline tells you what it is, what it holds and what's been done to it, without being selected. This page is the key to those marks. Each mark's control has its own page, linked from here.

<AtAGlance where="The timeline's lanes" tools={['set_selection', 'set_audio']} />

<Shot
  name="04-editor.window"
  alt="The editor with four tracks on the timeline: a green audio clip with its waveform and a white volume line, two teal clips for a shape and a graphic, and an amber text clip. Each clip has its name in a darker strip along the top with a small symbol for its kind, and the playhead runs through every track."
/>

## The clip block

Each clip draws as one block with 2 pt rounded corners and a thin border, so you can always see where one clip ends and the next begins.

From top to bottom, a block holds its name strip, its action lane if it has actions, its filmstrip and its waveform. The filmstrip and the waveform sit under a wash of the clip's own colour, so a clip reads as one coloured object rather than a row of photographs.

The action lane shows a band for each [action](/motion/action-lane/). The selected action's span is also washed down the whole clip, in the action colour: mint in the dark look, a deeper green in the light one.

## Colour by kind

A clip's colour and the symbol on its name strip tell you its kind.

| Kind | Colour | Symbol |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Video | Slate | A strip of film |
| Audio | Green | A waveform |
| Image | Violet | A photo |
| Freeze frame | Violet | A snowflake |
| Text | Amber | Letters |
| Shape | Teal | A square on a circle |
| Graphic | Teal | Curly braces |
| Nest | Grey | A stack of squares |
| Adjustment | Rose | Overlapping filter circles |

The kind comes from what the clip shows, not only from its file. A video file's clip with its picture switched off reads as audio, in green with the waveform symbol. That's how the sound half of a [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) pair looks.

A [label](/timeline/names-and-labels/) never changes the block's colour, because the colour says what the clip is and a label is something you said about it.

## The name strip

The darker strip along the top of a clip carries, from left to right, its kind symbol, a link symbol if it's [linked](#linked-clips), its name, a wave if it has a During motion, and its label dot.

A clip with a name of its own shows that. Otherwise it shows what it holds: a nest's name, the file's name, the text itself, or the shape's kind. A clip with none of those reads as its kind, such as **Graphic** or **Adjustment**. A name too long for the strip ends in an ellipsis.

On a narrow clip the strip gives things up from the right. The kind symbol stays longest, and the dot and the wave are left out when they'd run into it.

### The label dot

A labelled clip shows a small dot in its label colour at the right end of the name strip. See [Clip names and labels](/timeline/names-and-labels/).

### Motion marks

Two small marks show a clip's active [motion presets](/motion/motion-presets/):

- **A wedge** along the bottom of the name strip, from the left end for an In preset and from the right end for an Out preset. It's as long as the preset's duration at the current zoom, and it rises towards its inner end, so you can see how far into the clip the motion runs. It's never shorter than 2 pt or wider than the clip.
- **A small wave** at the right end of the strip, just left of the label dot, for a During movement.

A detached sound half shows neither, even though it holds a copy of the picture's settings.

## Picture and sound

### Filmstrip

Thumbnails run along the picture part of a video, image or freeze frame clip, each 34 pt wide and cropped to fill its tile.

Each thumbnail is the source frame at that point in the clip, to the nearest earlier whole second of the source, and it follows the clip's trims, speed, reverse and speed ramps. A filmstrip of a log, PQ or HLG file shows the converted picture, not the flat image in the file.

Text, shape, graphic, nest and adjustment clips have no thumbnails.

### Waveform

A clip with sound draws it as a waveform, below the filmstrip when the clip has both. The waveform follows the clip's source time through speed changes and ramps.

The waveform draws faded when the clip or its track is muted, or when another track's solo silences it. A track's mute button stays unlit under another track's solo, so the waveform is the place to look to see what's in the mix. See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/) and [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/).

### Filling in after import

Filmstrips and waveforms are made once for each file and kept with the project, so they fill in a moment after you add a file. See [On-device media analysis](/projects/media-analysis/).

## Lines over a clip

Up to four thin lines show how a clip changes over time. All of them are read off the clip as it plays, and each has its own control.

### The volume line

A thin white line over the waveform shows the level you hear from the clip, with its volume, fades, ducking and volume actions folded in. The top of the audio part is +30 dB and the bottom is −60 dB, and a silenced clip's line lies along the bottom. Small squares in the action colour mark where a volume action ends.

Nest clips don't draw it. To change the level from the timeline, see [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/).

### The duck line

A thin yellow line over a clip set to duck by speech shows where the rest of the mix goes down and comes back. The top of the audio part is the mix at full level and the bottom is silence.

A duck set to **Clip Length** draws no line, because it lasts as long as the clip. See [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/).

### The Hide While Silent line

A teal line across the picture part of a clip with [Hide While Silent](/effects/hide-while-silent/) on shows where the clip fades out in each pause and back in before speech. The top is fully shown and the bottom is fully hidden.

### The rate line

A clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) draws its rate as a white line with a dark edge across its action lane, here and in the Clip tab's lane. The bottom of the lane is the clip's own slowest rate and the top its fastest, so a small ramp looks as tall as a big one. Read the numbers in the Speed section.

The timeline draws it at the Medium and Large [track heights](/timeline/track-height/), not at Small.

## Fade handles

Small white squares at the top corners of a clip's audio part set its fades. Drag one inward to fade in or out. The square sits at the corner with no fade, and at the end of the fade once there is one.

The fade's length snaps to whole frames and stops at the clip's length. It doesn't snap to clip edges. The handles write the same two values as the Fades section, so see [Audio fades](/audio/fades/) for the rest.

## The transition zone

The overlap between two clips draws as a hatched zone with a solid edge down each side. The transition's kind is written in it when the whole word fits. On a short transition the word is left out, and the [Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/) still names it. See [Transitions](/motion/transitions/).

## Selected clips

A selected clip gets a 2 pt coral ring, and most commands act on it. When the clip is wide enough to trim and its track is unlocked, it also shows a trim grip at each end. See [Select clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/).

## Linked clips

A picture and the sound Detach Audio split from it each show a link symbol after their kind symbol. Select one and the other gets a dashed ring in your Mac's accent colour, because edits to one move both. See [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/).

## Dimmed clips

A clip draws dimmed when its track is hidden, or when both its picture and its sound are switched off. A muted clip isn't dimmed. Only its waveform fades.

## Adjustment clips

An [adjustment clip](/color/adjustment-clips/) is a plain rose block with only its name strip and action lane. It has no filmstrip or waveform, and its track is as tall as a picture track.

## Good to know

- A short track leaves marks out. The filmstrip needs 10 pt of height, the waveform, duck line and Hide While Silent line 8 pt, the fade handles 10 pt and the volume line 12 pt. A text clip at the Small [track height](/timeline/track-height/) is little more than its name strip.
- A [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/) draws a faint hatch across its whole lane, over its clips. Clips on it show no trim grips.
- On a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/), clips draw at half strength with a dashed outline.
- Inside an open [nest](/editing/nests/), a Hide While Silent line that reads its sound from outside the nest isn't drawn, though the clip still fades.

## Related

- [Clip names and labels](/timeline/names-and-labels/)
- [Track height](/timeline/track-height/)
- [Action bands and the action lane](/motion/action-lane/)

---
title: The ruler and playhead
description: Read the timeline's time ruler, scrub along it, and see how the playhead decides where edits land.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The ruler is the strip of time above the tracks. The playhead marks one moment on it: the frame the preview shows, and the point where most edits land.

<AtAGlance where="The ruler above the timeline's tracks" tools="set_playhead" />

## The playhead

The playhead is the coral line down every track, with a triangle head on the ruler. It always sits on a frame.

## Scrub on the ruler

Click the ruler to move the playhead there, and drag along it to scrub. Pressing on the ruler pauses playback, and it stays paused when you let go.

While you scrub, you hear the sound under the playhead. The press plays a short piece of it, and so does each new frame the drag reaches. See [Hear a scrub](/audio/scrub-audio/).

The scrub [snaps](/timeline/snapping/) like any other drag. Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> as you press to scrub without snapping.

A press within 6 pt of a marker's flag takes the [marker](/timeline/markers/), not the ruler, so start the scrub just beside it.

## Lane clicks

A click in a lane doesn't move the playhead. On empty space it starts a [marquee selection](/timeline/selecting-clips/), and a plain click there clears the selection.

## The edit point

These commands work at the playhead, so put it where you want the edit first:

| Command | Key |
| --- | --- |
| **Clip ▸ Split** | <kbd>⌘T</kbd> |
| **Clip ▸ Trim Start to Playhead** | <kbd>W</kbd> |
| **Clip ▸ Trim End to Playhead** | <kbd>E</kbd> |
| **Clip ▸ Freeze Frame** | <kbd>⇧⌘F</kbd> |
| **Edit ▸ Paste** | <kbd>⌘V</kbd> |
| **Edit ▸ Insert at Playhead** | |
| **Edit ▸ Overwrite at Playhead** | |

To place the playhead exactly, [step by frames](/timeline/playback/#step-frames) or [jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/).

## Ticks and labels

The ruler's ticks adapt to the zoom. Zoomed in, they mark single frames. As you zoom out, they step through 2, 5 and 10 frames, then 1, 2, 5, 10, 15 and 30 seconds, then 1, 2, 5, 10, 15 and 30 minutes, and at the widest one hour.

Labels use the project's timecode format, **Frames** or **Milliseconds**, set in [the Document tab](/projects/background-and-timecode/). A timeline under an hour long drops the leading `00:` from its labels so they fit.

The ruler also carries [markers](/timeline/markers/), the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) and the selected [action's](/motion/action-lane/) span. Inside an open [nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/), it counts from the nest's own start.

## Following the playhead

The timeline scrolls itself to keep the playhead in view, during playback and after a jump. When the playhead comes within 24 pt of either edge of the visible part, or leaves it, the view moves so the playhead sits about a third of the way in.

## With an agent

`set_playhead` moves the playhead and the preview, in silence. It isn't an edit, so there's nothing to undo. An agent that splits, freezes a frame or adds a marker without giving a time works at the playhead. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/).

## Related

- [Play, pause and shuttle](/timeline/playback/)
- [Jump around the timeline](/timeline/move-the-playhead/)
- [Zoom and scroll the timeline](/timeline/zoom-and-scroll/)
- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)

6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	The ruler is the strip of time above the tracks. The playhead marks one moment on it: the frame the preview shows, and the point where most edits land.
9	
10	<AtAGlance where="The ruler above the timeline's tracks" tools="set_playhead" />
11	
12	## The playhead
13	
14	The playhead is the coral line down every track, with a triangle head on the ruler. A click or a drag lands it on a frame.
15	
16	## Scrub on the ruler
17	
18	Click the ruler to move the playhead there, and drag along it to scrub. Pressing on the ruler pauses playback, and it stays paused when you let go.
19	
20	While you scrub, you hear the sound under the playhead. The press plays a short piece of it, and so does each new frame the drag reaches. See [Hear a scrub](/audio/scrub-audio/).
21	
22	The scrub [snaps](/timeline/snapping/) like any other drag. Hold <kbd>⌘</kbd> as you press to scrub without snapping.
23	
24	A press within 6 pt of a marker's flag takes the [marker](/timeline/markers/), not the ruler, so start the scrub beside it.
25	
26	## Lane clicks
27	
28	A click in a lane doesn't move the playhead. On empty space it starts a [marquee selection](/timeline/selecting-clips/), and a plain click there clears the selection.
29	
30	## The edit point
31	
32	These commands work at the playhead, so put it where you want the edit first:
